ii

TP Growth Marketing Blueprint

PDF p. 5

Growth Marketers are responsible for generating qualified pipeline by engaging the brand´s customer/prospect base to inform, educate, influence, and persuade them towards a purchase decision.

TP’s Growth Marketing teams are focused on Account-Based Everything (ABX), a strategic, account-centric approach where marketing resources are allocated to top target accounts. ABX integrates multi-touch attribution, account-level engagement scoring, and buying committee mapping across all go-to-market activities to drive measurable pipeline impact and revenue attribution. In practice, this means Growth Marketing, Sales (BD’s), and SDRs (VAMs, Inside Sales, and any other regional BDR teams) all work together on the same set of accounts and coordinate outreach across channels.

The following Growth Marketing blueprint is supported by four key growth principles:

1Be data driven
2Do fewer activities with higher impact
3Become more efficient and effective each quarter
4Grow sales and trust internally
1

Key official sales funnel definitions

PDF p. 5–15

I. Lead vs Contact

A lead is a business prospect that may or may not be interested in TP’s services. Leads can come from unknown companies (no prior relationship with TP) or known companies (existing prospects or clients in TP's system from new buying centers for a different line of business (LOB)) and require further qualification to determine their level of interest. Within ABX target accounts, leads are also evaluated based on their role within the buying committee and the overall account engagement.

Conversely, a contact is someone who has already been identified and detailed information has been gathered about their interests and specific business needs. Contacts are individuals with whom the Business Development (BD) team has already met, established a relationship, and identified as potential customers with defined needs. BDs convert only qualified leads (Sales Accepted Leads) into contacts so they can be tied to Opportunities.

While leads and contacts may seem similar, they serve different purposes and must be handled differently. The key distinction: leads sit in marketing's pipeline until qualified; contacts are known stakeholders within target accounts. Marketing, Sales, and SDRs will actively conduct coordinated outreach, market to, and nurture leads and contacts, scoring from zero through to SAL in Marketo, account-attached from time of being added to Salesforce. BDs will add campaign codes, instead of contacts, to opportunities to attribute pipeline and revenue to marketing campaigns. Automation will add campaign code-associated contacts to the tagged opportunity through Salesforce Campaign Influence 2.0 and Salesforce Flow for marketing attribution purposes.

II. Lead Qualification

Lead qualification in growth marketing is the process of assessing whether a lead that has shown interest in TP services is likely to become a valuable customer. The goal is to prioritize leads that are most likely to convert, ensuring that the sales team focuses on the best opportunities.

Based on their interaction with marketing activities, leads are assessed as having either sufficient interest to pursue a potential deal, or not.

a) Lead Source

A lead source is the original channel through which a lead first learns about TP. Understanding and preserving the original lead source is crucial because it helps to identify which channels are most effective in attracting high-quality leads, allowing for better allocation of marketing resources.

The lead source in Salesforce must remain as the original and cannot be altered. Leads and contacts that originate from marketing efforts are termed marketing generated.

Lead Nurturing

Leads can be further influenced through Marketing Nurturing Campaigns, regardless of their initial source. The purpose of nurturing campaigns is to provide relevant, valuable content and personalized interactions. This approach helps sustain engagement, build trust, and advance leads toward making a purchasing decision, or ensure that TP remains top of mind for clients. All lead sources below count towards Marketing Nurturing Campaigns.

b) Lead Qualification by Growth Marketing

Growth Marketing qualifies leads by using the field Lead Stage in Salesforce. Lead Stage refers to the phases a potential customer goes through in the funnel, from initial awareness to becoming a qualified prospect. Each stage represents how far a lead is in the journey, helping marketing and sales track progress and determine the next steps for nurturing the relationship.

SuspectMQLSQLSAL
SuspectMQL (Marketing Qualified Lead)SQL (Sales Qualified Lead)SAL (Sales Accepted Lead)
A suspect is a potential customer who has been identified as a potential fit for TP’ services but has not yet shown any interest.An MQL is a lead that has shown interest in TP through marketing activities and qualified for marketing nurturing but is not yet ready to talk to sales or make a purchase.An SQL is a lead that has either reached a 60+ qualification score through marketing nurturing, or has demonstrated direct buying intent (e.g., submitting an RFP/RFI request, filling out the Contact Us form, or agreeing to meet).An SAL is a lead that the sales team has accepted from the marketing team, indicating that: - Met the lead. - Have a legit business opportunity
MQLs must have the right job title (or role) and the right company size for the region (minimum company size differs by region). If this rule is not fulfilled, the lead must not be categorized as MQL. Note: While lead qualification is currently tracked at the individual level in Salesforce (MQL), our ABX strategy is evolving toward account-level qualification (MQA), where engagement is measured across the buying committee. Using automation, we will track qualification both at the individual and account level.Marketing teams must send only warm leads to sales; once a lead is categorized as SQL, the person should be passed to the SDR/BD, and the SDR/BD is expected to contact and qualify the lead.Just because a BD has spoken to a person does NOT automatically qualify the lead as a SAL. Once a lead is accepted, it is expected that the BD converts the lead into a contact and tag it to an opportunity and company.
In Salesforce, in the Lead Stage, you can select Suspect.In Salesforce, in the Lead Stage, you can select MQL (Marketing Qualified Lead).In Salesforce, in the Lead Stage, you can select SQL (Sales Qualified Lead)In Salesforce, the Lead Stage is changed to SAL and the Lead Status is marked as Accepted.

In Salesforce, the lead stage field is located under the section called Qualification by Growth Marketing.

Scenarios by stage

Scenarios: Suspect

Scenarios include:

  • Being a member of the Executive LinkedIn Campaign
  • Social media comments or likes
  • Sharing social media posts
  • Accepting LinkedIn connections
  • Receiving a list of attendees from a vendor at an industry event or trade show, where the individuals had no interaction with TP
  • Opened an email
  • Record added as a result of lead mapping or received from the source/database without previous interaction with TP (Intent Marketing, ZoomInfo, Apollo, and SalesNav)
Scenarios: Marketing Qualified Lead (MQL)

Scenarios include:

  • Registered for a TP Physical Event or TP Virtual Event
  • Attended a TP Physical Event or TP Virtual Event
  • Clicked on the link in an email
  • Filled out a web form to download TP content
  • On LinkedIn, viewed /clicked a TP Smart Link page, but have not yet agreed to meet
  • Accepting a LinkedIn connection by Lead Agency / BD (only if it is a customized message)
  • 3rd Party Event: People who stopped by our booth and/or gave us their contact info, and/or expressed interest in talking. (Submitting their business cards for a raffle or the attendee list should NOT be marked as MQLs.)
Scenarios: Sales Qualified Lead (SQL)

Scenarios include:

  • Scored 60 or above.
  • Filled out the Contact Us form on the TP Website (since SDR/BDs take these leads directly, Marketing has no way of determining title or company size – so Web Leads are automatically listed as SQL)
  • They agreed to meet with TP. NOTE: This invitation to meet could have come via email, extended during a webinar, on LinkedIn, or in person
  • If someone contacts us (through any channel) and invites us to participate in an RFP, the BD contacts the person
  • LinkedIn InMail or Email Value conversation (Exchange of messages meant to uncover or determine the amount of value that you might create for the client, and therefore what fair compensation for you would be. During this conversation, you may find more information about the prospect such us budget, sense of urgency, current providers / competitors, as well as pain points.)

Scenarios: Sales Accepted Lead (SAL)

These leads should also be added to a different flow to ensure that they are nurtured separately from new leads. However, if a meeting occurs, and the BD sees potential (meaning, it’s the right company size and the right title), BUT the timing is wrong. The Lead Stage is changed to MQL, and the Lead Status is changed to Recycled, and Marketing / the BD continues to nurture them through a separate communication and messaging flow. Recycling a lead also triggers an automatic score adjustment based on the selected recycle reason to ensure accurate re‑entry into the nurturing cycle. Refer to XI. No MeetingIf no meeting is held, the Lead Stage is changed back to MQL, the Lead Status is changed to Recycle, and Marketing continues to nurture them.—

The initial Lead Status must be set to Open, as sales are not expected to engage with Suspects immediately. Suspects may also be marked as Rejected, Recycled, or Archived, if they meet the appropriate criteria.The initial Lead Status must be set to Open, as sales are not expected to engage with MQL (Marketing Qualified Lead) immediately. MQLs may also be marked as Rejected, Recycled, or Archived, if they meet the appropriate criteria.Once a lead is classified as an SQL (Sales Qualified Lead), it should be handed over to the BD who is responsible for contacting and qualifying the lead. The Lead Status should be updated from Open to Contacted once the BD gets in contact with the lead. Archived³: Archived leads are NOT always Sales Accepted Lead (SAL). Leads can be archived as a result of inactivity. Leads archived in September 2024 followed the following characteristics: - No activities after September 2022 - No Campaign engaged after Sept 2022 - No changes to the owner or any other information.

³ Archived leads are NOT always Sales Accepted Lead (SAL).

IV. Lead Creation in Salesforce

To create a lead in Salesforce, follow these steps:

  • From the top menu, click on the Lead tab.
  • Select New Lead.
  • A new window will appear with the required fields for creating a lead. Complete the needed information. For the Marketing team, it's essential to include the Existing Company in Salesforce if the company is already listed.
  • After filling in all the necessary information, click Save.

Marketing campaigns

PDF p. 15–24

V. Campaign Hierarchies Organize Your Campaigns

A campaign hierarchy in Salesforce is a way to organize and manage marketing efforts by structuring campaigns in a tiered format.

The purpose of a campaign hierarchy in Salesforce is to organize and manage related marketing efforts under a unified structure, making it easier to track performance and optimize strategies. This approach ensures that all campaigns are aligned with broader marketing goals and can be adjusted as needed for better results.

  • Parent Campaign: The top-level campaign represents a broad marketing initiative. At TP, we refer to these main campaigns as "strategies" (e.g., "Travel & Hospitality Strategy").
  • Child-Campaign: Smaller, related campaigns related to specific activities under the main campaign (e.g., "Physical Event” and "Trade Show").

Here are some examples of campaign hierarchies to illustrate this concept:

North America operates the same way. NA uses the same hierarchy, and adds ABM as an additional strategy: an ABM grandparent sits alongside the Strategy grandparents, with the motion as the parent and its tactics underneath. Any campaign SDRs work gets two Inside Sales children, one Enterprise and one Mid-Market, because different SDR teams work them.
NA naming: 202X.X TP USA - Campaign Type - Campaign Detail, with plain hyphens. The month comes from the start date (2026.9, not 2026.09), the type matches the Salesforce Type field, and the detail never repeats the vertical (the grandparent carries it). A start date outside the grandparent window can’t roll up. Marketing Ops creates grandparents.

A new window will pop -up.

XI. Marketing Lead Scoring

Lead scoring determines prospect’s sales-readiness based on the interest they show in TP business and their overall company fit. Scoring can start at any point throughout the lead’s lifecycle depending on the urgency and interest level. A stage titled “Suspect” holds incoming prospects as they enter revenue cycle. We may want to push some of them straight to sales. For the rest, we use engagement tactics like email, events, paid ads to nurture them, until they reach 60+ score and become sales-ready – SQL. As soon as lead reaches qualification score, it’s assigned to SDR/BD for proactive personalized outreach and qualification.

The lead scoring system described below uses demographic and firmographic (explicit) attributes, such as company industry, and job title, as well as behavioral (implicit) scoring, such as clicks, form fill outs, and web visits. The goal is to identify which leads are ready to move to sales and which leads require further nurturing.

Note: Leads can also receive negative points for actions that indicate the lead is not a great fit. When lead is Recycled, its score is reset to “15” to regain their behavior score as a result as new cycle of marketing nurturing and become an SQL again.
40Global → local marketing handoff (see Lead Ownership)
60+SQL: assigned to SDR/BD
15Recycled score reset

Recycled Lead Scoring

When a lead is set to Recycled status with a score of 60 or higher (SQL threshold), its score is recalculated so it re-enters the nurturing cycle with the right qualification level.

The adjusted score depends on the Recycle Reason selected by the BD/SDR:

Recycle ReasonScore UpdateReason
Left Company=0Individual is no longer a valid prospect and must re-enter as a new lead.
No Response / No Show-15 pointsReflects lack of engagement while preserving partial behavioral relevance.
Do not want to work with TP · In-house or working with Competitor · This is not the right time= 15Ensures re-entry into early-stage nurturing without triggering SQL status prematurely.

After the score adjustment:

  1. The Lead Stage is automatically updated to MQL.
  2. A notification is sent to the respective regional marketing POC, informing them that the lead has been recycled, including the updated score and the lead details required for continued nurturing.
The example recycled-lead alert email is shown in the PDF (p. 28). It isn't reproduced here because the screenshot contains a prospect's personal details.

This ensures consistent global handling of recycled leads, accurate scoring governance, and timely handoff to regional marketing teams for re-engagement.

a. Lead Ownership

As part of the lead scoring system, marketers will assume responsibility for leads that are not yet ready to be passed on to sales executives. This approach ensures that leads receive a thorough qualification and nurturing, so they are fully prepared for meaningful engagement by the time they are handed off to sales. The goal is to enhance lead quality, making the transition to sales more seamless and improving conversion rates.

For leads generated through global activities, the global marketing team will nurture them until they reach a score of 40. At this point, the leads will be transferred to local marketing teams for continued engagement. Local marketers will receive an email notification when a lead reaches a score of 40 or higher, providing the lead's key information and a clear call to action (CTA) and confirming that the lead has been assigned to them.

The objective for local marketers is to qualify these leads further, driving them to a score of 60, at which stage they will be ready to move into the sales pipeline. This structured process helps ensure that leads are consistently cultivated and passed on at the optimal time.

The example 40-point alert email is shown in the PDF (p. 29). It isn't reproduced here because the screenshot contains a prospect's personal details.

When a lead is assigned to someone else in Salesforce, the new owner will receive a notification in the top right corner of their Salesforce Home, alerting them to the new lead.

XII. Understanding Email Event Logging

When sending emails, Marketo logs different data points to the person’s activity logs. Here are the basic ones.

EventDescription
SentIs logged every time an email is sent from the Marketo servers regardless of if it is actually delivered. Bounced emails are still logged as “Sent.”
DeliveredIs logged every time an email is accepted by the recipient mail server. This does not mean it avoided spam filters. There can only be 1 delivery for each sent email.
Hard BouncedSome hard bounces are a result of spam blocks, so we won’t try to email that person for 24 hours again in any campaign. Other hard bounces like non-existent inboxes are permanent, and we will never email the person again from any campaign.
Soft BouncedIs logged when a server response is unclear, mailbox full or general server issues. We do put these people through a retry logic for 24-36 hours for potential future delivery. This does not disqualify the person from other mailings.
OpenedIs logged when a recipient views an email with images NOT blocked. Only one open event per email, per person, per smart campaign is logged. If they open the same email from their inbox twice, it will not be logged more than once.
ClickedIs logged every time a decorated URL from the email is loaded in the browser (the result of clicking the link). Usually this is the recipient clicking but can also be a cut/paste.
UnsubscribedIs logged when a person clicks on the unsubscribe link of an email and submits the unsubscribe form.

XIII. Campaign Landing Pages

Growth marketing teams are using different platforms to launch and maintain campaign landing pages such as Instapage, Cvent, or Marketo. In TP North America, specific instructions for Cvent and Marketo landing pages can be found on the US Marketing SharePoint.

For regions using the Instapage platform, the form should be integrated with Marketo to automatically track performance in Marketo and SDFC. The form must also meet the minimum field requirements outlined in Section IV: Lead Creation in Salesforce, presented in this document.

Instapage Platform

To set up the form, navigate to the "Integrations" section of the settings and select Marketo. After logging in with the appropriate credentials and selecting the correct API, choose the desired Marketo list. This list must already be part of the Marketo flow connected to the Salesforce campaign.

Once connected, there will be an option to map the fields from the Instapage form to the corresponding fields in Marketo. Each field from the form should be carefully matched to the appropriate field in Marketo.

Refer to the field matching table to identify and match relevant fields in Marketo. (Note: The names of Instapage fields may vary depending on the wording or language of the form.)

Instapage FieldsMarketo Fields
First NameFirst Name
Last NameLast Name
Your RoleJob Title

Company EmailEmail

After completing the mapping, clicking the “Finish” button and republishing the landing page is necessary.

Finally, it is crucial to test the integration to ensure that submissions are correctly sent to Marketo and Salesforce and that all data is captured accurately. This integration enables seamless data transfer between Instapage, Marketo, and Salesforce through effective form field mapping.

Connecting Domain and Subdomain (if not done yet):

For publishing landing pages, the domain to use is TP.com. If a new is required, reach out to the IT team and request a DNS record creation.

Once the domain is created, follow these steps to connect it:

  1. In your workspace, go to Settings and select Connect Domain.
  2. In the registrar section, select Continue.
  3. Enter TP.com as the main domain.
  4. For the subdomain, enter the specific subdomain you are creating (e.g., enter travel for travel.TP.com).
  5. For DNS setup, select Continue.
  6. In the connection setup, select Close.

It may take up to 48 hours for the system to recognize the site. Check the domain’s connection status by going to Settings > Domains, searching for CNAME, and reviewing Connection Status:

  • Connected: The landing page is ready for matching.
  • Waiting SSL: Allow 24–36 hours for SSL to propagate.
  • If delays continue, IT can contact systems to expedite registration.

To match the domain with a landing page:

  1. Under Landing Pages, locate the page you want to publish.
  2. Select Publish Page.
  3. Choose Custom Domain and pick the created DNS record from Your Domain list.
  4. Add the extension (e.g., travel.TP.com/beyond-the-recovery). Avoid using only the DNS record directly.
  5. Select Publish.

Best Practices:

  • Cloning landing pages should be avoided, as this can also clone integration settings and Instapage lead alerts, potentially causing issues with lead management.
  • Testing integrations with existing and new records in Salesforce is important to ensure that all fields function as intended and identify which fields are required.
  • As TP is a GDPR-compliant company, ensuring that the form includes the required disclaimers is necessary.
  • It is essential to connect the landing page to the correct Marketo list in the flow; using the wrong list may result in records being added to an incorrect flow.

XIV. Marketo Bot Activity Detection

Sometimes, email bot activity can erroneously inflate your email opens and clicks data. To avoid this, please add the following Marketo Bot Activity Detection constraint to the Open and Click updaters for all email campaigns.

  1. Open your program
  2. Select Open / Click updater
  3. Open Smart List
  4. Click in “Add Constraint”
  5. Choose “Is Bot Activity”
  6. Choose “False”

Sales Development Representatives (SDRs)

PDF p. 35–40

The primary purpose of the Sales Development Representatives (SDRs) or Presales Specialists are to accelerate the sales engine by identifying, qualifying, and nurturing high-potential leads until they are sales-ready. By bridging the gap between initial interest and a formal sales cycle, SDRs empower Business Development Managers (BDs) to focus on high-value closing activities, effectively shortening the overall deal lifecycle. SDRs (e.g., VAMs, Inside Sales, and any other regional BDR teams) are strategic partners to the BDs, providing continuous support throughout the deal to ensure momentum is maintained and opportunities are developed faster through rigorous qualification and persistent relationship management.

Core Responsibilities

ResponsibilityDetail
Account TargetingStrategic logos are identified through a variety of high-intent channels to ensure the pipeline is always primed. Sources include: BD-Driven Targets: Collaboration with Business Development Managers to pursue specific high-value prospects (the primary source). · Demandbase & Intent Data: Leveraging accounts showing high engagement levels or relevant market activity. · Salesforce History: Revisiting and re-engaging logos from past interactions to breathe new life into dormant opportunities. · Marketing & Central Strategy: Aligning with global business goals and specific marketing campaign outputs.
Strategic Pairing & Account AssignmentSDRs are directly paired with BDs to work as a unified team. While some SDRs may focus on specific industry verticals, the primary driver for assignment is the partnership with the BD. Together, they develop and execute a shared plan for their assigned logos to develop deals faster.
Research & Lead IdentificationSDRs conduct thorough research on the assigned accounts to identify potential leads. This involves connecting the dots within the organization to find key decision-makers, understanding the company’s needs, and uncovering any existing relationships or opportunities.
Lead Qualification & OutreachOnce leads are identified and qualified based on their potential to engage with our services, the SDRs initiate outreach efforts. This involves a multichannel approach using soft skills and TP knowledge and understanding for targeted engagement. This includes emails, phone calls, LinkedIn messages, invites to TP virtual and in-person events, and other relevant communication channels, to engage the leads and introduce TP’s offerings.
Exploratory Meeting SchedulingAfter successfully engaging a lead, the SDR schedules an exploratory meeting. This meeting is attended by the SDR and the BDs, who delve deeper into the client’s needs, challenges, and potential opportunities for collaboration.
Continuous BD SupportSDRs provide end-to-end support, assisting BDs throughout the entire deal process by managing follow-ups, gathering additional stakeholder data, and keeping the prospect engaged during complex procurement phases
Relationship NurturingIf an opportunity is not immediately identified during the exploratory meeting, the SDRs continue to nurture the relationship. This involves regular follow-ups, providing value through insights or resources, and staying top-of-mind with the lead until the right opportunity arises. The goal is to maintain and grow the relationship, ensuring that when a need does emerge, TP is the first partner they consider.

XV. SDRs and Lead Management

Effective lead management is the engine of our growth strategy. It ensures that the TP sales organization maintains a high-velocity pipeline, optimizes resource allocation, and captures every viable market opportunity. Our process is designed to proactively drive engagement and shorten the deal lifecycle.

PrincipleHow
Strategic Lead Capture & QualificationWe adopt a sophisticated approach to lead entry that prioritizes long-term relationship value over immediate transaction: Broad-Spectrum Entry: Leads are integrated into Salesforce based on their strategic relevance to TP’s footprint. We do not limit our CRM to immediate "BANT" qualified opportunities; rather, we capture any entity where a high-value partnership can be explored. · Intent-Based Qualification: Once in the ecosystem, SDRs assess leads based on organizational fit, engagement signals (via Demandbase), and potential synergy with TP’s global service offerings. · Relationship Mapping: We focus on understanding the prospective client’s ecosystem—identifying key stakeholders and latent pain points—to move beyond a cold outreach and toward a strategic partnership.
High-Fidelity Lead Tracking & VisibilityTo ensure a "no-lead-left-behind" culture, we utilize Salesforce as our single source of truth: Omnichannel Logging: Every touchpoint—from LinkedIn engagement to event invitations—is registered within dedicated campaigns. · Auditability: This level of tracking provides leadership with full visibility into the effort-to-outcome ratio, allowing for data-driven adjustments to our outreach strategy.
Dynamic PrioritizationSDRs and BDs employ a "Tiered Engagement" model to ensure that our most valuable resources are focused where they will have the most impact: High-Propensity Scoring: Leads are prioritized based on a combination of intent data, historical interactions, and BD feedback. · Accelerated Response: High-priority leads trigger a "fast-track" outreach protocol to capitalize on momentum and develop deals faster.
Continuous Pipeline Optimization (The Review Cycle)The SDR-BD partnership is governed by regular cadence reviews to prevent pipeline stagnation: Velocity Analysis: We identify and remove bottlenecks that delay the transition from "Lead" to "Opportunity." · Strategic Pivot: If a lead is not ready for an immediate RFP, the SDR shifts to a nurturing posture, ensuring TP remains the incumbent choice when the procurement window eventually opens.

XVI. SDRs and Salesforce

At TP, Salesforce serves as our Single Source of Truth (SSoT). It is the strategic infrastructure that enables seamless SDR-BD collaboration, ensures pipeline transparency, and provides the data-driven insights necessary to optimize our market go-to-market strategy.

AreaDetail
High-Fidelity Activity IntelligenceWe move beyond simple "logging" to capture Strategic Interaction Data. Every outreach—whether via LinkedIn, telephony, or high-touch email—is documented to build a comprehensive history of the prospect’s journey. Institutional Memory: By capturing every touchpoint, we ensure that no context is lost during the SDR-to-BD handover or during long-term nurturing cycles. · Velocity Analytics: Rigorous tracking allows leadership to analyze "Time-to-Engagement" metrics, identifying which outreach sequences are most effective at shortening the deal lifecycle.
Precision Campaign ManagementTo maintain a high-velocity pipeline, SDRs utilize dynamic Campaign Member Status tracking. This ensures that the momentum of every lead is visible in real-time, allowing for surgical prioritization of follow-ups.
Future State: Intelligent Process AutomationIn early 2026, we are transitioning toward a zero-friction data environment through Salesforce Flow automation. This evolution will eliminate manual overhead and enhance data integrity: Automated Attribution: Salesforce Flows will auto-update Campaign Member Status based on validated activities (e.g., Meeting Logged → Status: Meeting Held). · Real-Time ROI: Automated status updates ensure that Marketing and Sales leadership have an instantaneous view of campaign performance and attribution, removing the lag of manual entry and ensuring total alignment with global business objectives.

XVIII. Monthly Growth Marketing Report

The Global Growth Marketing Report is structured around three primary pillars.

PillarWhat it measures
Lead GenerationThis pillar assesses our ability to generate leads from various marketing activities. This is measured by the time stamp of each stage.
Lead QualityThe dashboard monitors lead quality through the conversion to Marketing Qualified Leads (MQL), Sales Qualified Leads (SQL) and Sales Accepted Leads (SAL).
Impact on New BusinessIt monitors the marketing impact on New Business, whether in new geographies or lines of business within existing clients, or with entirely new clients.
The V10 of this Blueprint requires the implementation of Salesforce Campaign Influence 2.0 and associated business processes to accurately measure marketing attribution. As of the publishing of this version, these modules are not yet implemented and are expected to be completed within the 2027 Selling Season.
MeasurementDefinition
Opportunities MeasurementMarketing influence on new opportunities (pipeline) is measured by Created Date within the 16-month sales reporting period by Estimated Annualized Amount (EAA), using Campaign Influence 2.0 (multi-touch attribution), to measure total Return on Marketing Investment (ROMI). Credit is distributed across all marketing touchpoints that engaged the account prior to opportunity creation—including all contacts listed within the opportunity contact roles. This captures the true scope of marketing's pipeline contribution across the buying committee.
Closed Lost MeasurementMarketing influence on closed-lost opportunities is measured using Campaign Influence 2.0 (multi-touch attribution), applying the same credit distribution as open Opportunities. Closed-lost opportunities are reported by Created Date within the 16-month sales reporting period, measured by Estimated Annualized Amount (EAA). Production Start Date does not apply, as no production start occurs on an opportunity that was not awarded. Closed-lost reporting captures the full marketing-influenced pipeline regardless of outcome; it is not a measure of marketing performance against sales results for revenue attribution.
Wins MeasurementRevenue attribution is measured by Production Start Date within the 16-month sales reporting period via Campaign Influence 2.0 and Flow, crediting all marketing touchpoints across the account and buying committee. Opportunities and Wins are attributed based on influence percentage, not just primary contact, across all campaigns that touched the opportunity. Revenue attribution is based on closed-won opportunities (>90% probability) within the 16-month sales reporting period (September 1 – December 31), measured by Production Start Date and Signed and Produced Revenue (S+V). Credit applies to both: Marketing-Generated: Primary contact sourced by marketing measuring First Touch · Marketing-Influenced: Any contact role on the opportunity engaged with marketing touchpoints, but not sourced by Marketing, prior to close (Campaign Influence 2.0) measuring multi-touch attribution. This multi-touch model captures marketing's full revenue and pipeline impact across the account—not just first-touch attribution. In addition, it tracks the progress Month by Month and by source.

Attribution Model: Even Distribution (Interim)

Campaign Influence 2.0 will launch in Q3 2026 using even distribution, allocating equal credit across all marketing touchpoints prior to opportunity creation. This is an interim model, adopted because insufficient closed-won history exists to support a statistically valid custom weighting.

Scope limitation: Even distribution data will be used for directional tracking only, not as a benchmark for budget allocation or program investment decisions during this interim period. It will be used to establish baseline touchpoint volume and engagement patterns across the pipeline. Budget decisions will continue to rely on pipeline sourced/influenced volume and lead-to-SAL conversion rates as primary performance indicators.

Path to custom model: Given BPO enterprise deal cycles of 6–24 months, a time-based trigger alone is insufficient. Migration to a custom attribution model will be initiated when both of the following conditions are met:

  • Minimum 12 months of clean CI 2.0 data with consistent UTM tagging across all active campaigns
  • Minimum 50 CI 2.0-influenced closed-won opportunities to support statistically meaningful touchpoint analysis
  • Until both conditions are met, the even distribution model remains in effect, and reporting should be interpreted as directional, not definitive.
For the 2027 Selling Season, Marketing will align KPIs across geos for a one-time, 16-month period from Sep. 1, 2026, to Dec. 31, 2027 such that we align with Sales’ KPI measurement of 12 months (Jan. 1-Dec. 31) annually. This will enable Marketing to align with both measurement fields and timeframes so that Marketing reporting matches accurately to Sales reports and dashboards going forward.
